governanceNotes: D1 batch 74 (2026-09-26): premature-ejaculation DEFERRED without edges - CONSTITUTIVE-PROXIMITY (distress is a defining criterion) plus selection-on-definition and cross-sectional-only comorbidity evidence. Searched anchors: the Korean controlled cohort of 334 men with validated BDI and IIEF-EF instruments (PMID 21235722) documenting that self-assessed premature ejaculation carries depression and low self-esteem even after excluding erectile dysfunction, while strictly defined presumed cases show no excess psychological burden - the null for defined cases is carried openly as counterweight; the distress-focused clinic cohort (PMID 31024115) documenting lower-urinary-tract and depressive symptoms among men presenting for distressing early ejaculation (selection on the defining feature); the population-representative cohort of 3,001 men (PMID 40234544) documenting severity correlations of erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation with psychological-burden measures (cross-sectional, no direction). The located evidence measures psychological burden in samples selected or defined by distress, so an edge would register the defining feature as its own secondary outcome; mood comorbidity is directionally contested (performance anxiety precedes acquired cases) and the erectile-dysfunction comorbidity is described as a bidirectional cycle. Reopening: longitudinal incident-case cohorts with independently assessed mood outcomes, or directional comorbidity evidence.
